parties.counterparty: SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor)

plans.note: Article VIX carries the all-caps warranty disclaimer block; any damages exclusion/cap almost certainly sits in the same run of capitalized text (sec-p0112, sec-p0116) or immediately after in Article X. Check for one-sided exclusion of consequential damages and absence of a stated cap or carve-outs for confidentiality, IP infringement and willful misconduct.

No dedicated indemnity heading appears in the outline; scan Article X, the confidentiality article and the General Provisions catch-all (sec-p0144) before concluding it is missing. If only a Licensee-side indemnity exists, treat as deviation for lack of Licensor IP-infringement indemnity.

Article II (License Grant and Restrictions) and the Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation article are the likely homes of any restraint on our operating other FX platforms; also check FIELD OF USE in the definitions, which can function as a de facto non-compete.

The defined term 'Right of First Refusal' signals an exclusivity-type restraint on our sourcing; locate its operative clause (likely Article VIII or the pricing/commercial article) and check FIELD OF USE in Article I for exclusive-use language.

Pricing is set by the per-ticket volume tiers; no MFN language is signalled in the outline. Confirm around the tier table and Supplemental Payments definition that we owe the Licensor no best-terms undertaking before marking missing (MFN in our favour is optional, not required).

Article X is expressly captioned 'Confidential Information/Non Solicitation'. Check whether the non-solicit binds Licensee (likely mutual or one-sided against us), its duration, whether it reaches employees only or also customers/introducing brokers, and whether general advertising is carved out.

Term and termination are most likely in Article VIII (which follows the pricing tiers) with 'Initial Period' defined in Article I; confirm whether Licensee has notice-based exit without penalty and whether Licensor can terminate at will mid-term.

Look at the 'Initial Period' definition and the term article for automatic renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any renewal price uplift; note (not flag) a missing uplift cap or reminder mechanic.
Governing law, venue and any arbitration clause will sit in Article XXIV / General Provisions. New York is an accepted law; watch for foreign arbitration or an inconvenient exclusive venue.

Assignment and change-of-control language belongs in General Provisions (Article XXIV). Check for a bar on Licensee assignment to affiliates/successors and any Licensor termination right on our change of control; AFFILIATE is defined in Article I.

Article I defines DERIVATIVE WORK, INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS and MORAL RIGHTS; Article II will state ownership and any assignment to Licensor of feedback, configurations, customer/trading data or derivative works. Confirm our data and paid-for deliverables are not swept into Licensor ownership.

Article II is the grant clause; test scope against affiliate and contractor use (AFFILIATE, FIELD OF USE, LICENSED SOFTWARE/TECHNOLOGY definitions) and whether the grant is revocable at will or otherwise conditional.

Usage-verification or records-inspection rights against Licensee typically ride with the restrictions in Article II or the reporting/payment terms tied to the per-ticket tiers; also check General Provisions. Assess notice, frequency, cost allocation and on-site scope.

No penalty heading is visible; check the payment/pricing article for late-payment interest, shortfall penalties or 'Supplemental Payments' operating as liquidated damages against us. Service credits in our favour would not be flagged.

Article VIX is an express WARRANTY DISCLAIMER (merchantability, non-infringement, fitness, no assurance defects will be corrected). Likely a deviation for absence of any affirmative performance warranty or repair/re-perform remedy; check the maintenance obligations elsewhere for a substitute service-level commitment.
No insurance heading in the outline. Sweep General Provisions and the confidentiality article; if nothing, mark missing given the Licensor hosts the Platform and handles our trading data.

The volume tier table (US$7.50 down to US$5.00 per ticket) and the 'Supplemental Payments' / 'Market Day' definitions are where any minimum ticket volume, monthly minimum or take-or-pay shortfall would appear; confirm whether an exit or true-up-only remedy exists.

Check the termination article and General Provisions for post-termination wind-down, data return/deletion and migration assistance; Article II may instead require return or destruction of Licensed Software only, which does not satisfy this rule.
